threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the overground' when you're hopping between Dalston Junction and Hackney Central.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele version of 'Wonderwall.' Only in Brixton, right? Everyone just laughed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a saxophonist jamming outside Kottbusser Tor at midnight while a family of ducks waddled by. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a fountain with a DJ spining tunes, while kids at the playground laugh and dancers flow around. Pure Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate the BART delays without batting an eye—like dodging potholes on Mission St. It's part of the routine.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a Muni driver getting out to help a lost tourist. Only in SF could kindness shine through the chaos of delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the parks and plazas, but they miss the tiny bakeries with bread that still has a warm crust from the oven.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll know them by their overly careful navigation of the metro, clutching a paper map like it’s a treasure map, lost in plain sight.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the number of 'pop-up' cafes is just a trend, not a lifestyle choice. The locals speak in brunch menus.
Last night on the 196, a guy got on with a massive inflatable flamingo. The driver just shook his head and laughed, as if this was normal.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy expertly juggle apples while his friend rapped in front of the subway entrance. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand open at 3 AM serving currywurst with a side of techno beats blaring from the nearby bar.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their casual disdain for BART delays, while newcomers are still frantically checking their smartphones for updates.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 today, and a guy was reciting Shakespeare to a packed bus, totally drowned out by an opera singer nearby. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume the noise in Gràcia is just party vibes. They don’t realize it’s also the sound of artisans working late into the night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to use the 'bon dia' greeting; they still shy away from the local chatter before 10 AM.
